Meat grillers who visited for a family dinner at the end of the year.
While looking for a meat restaurant near Sharosu-gil, I chose it because of its good reviews and ratings, and I could immediately see why so many people visit it.

I ordered the basic set for 3 people and it consisted of pork belly, pork neck, and pork belly, so it was good for the family to eat. The pork belly was juicy without too much oil, and the neck meat was moist and not dry, so it was easy to eat with children.

The Jeongjeongsal was the most memorable because it had a balanced chewy texture and savory flavor. I was satisfied with the pork rind I ordered as it came out crispy and chewy without any unpleasant smell. I also liked that the charcoal scent was subtle and did not spoil the taste of the meat.

I was surprised by the sight of the steamed egg custard that I ordered in the middle, puffing up like a volcano, and it was so soft that it was good to eat between pieces of meat.
The kimchi stew was not spicy and the soup had depth, so it went well with the ending.'
Even though it was a weekday evening, the store was almost full, and the atmosphere was perfect for a company dinner or a family meal. This is a place I would like to visit again because the quality of meat, side dishes, and overall balance are all good.

The staff were friendly and took good care of the timing of grilling the meat and how to eat it, and the atmosphere of the store was comfortable, so I thought it would be a good place for a company dinner or date.

There is no reason to wait long

I visited around 6pm on a weekday and got in without waiting, but the waiting line quickly formed.

I ordered 2 pieces of special sirloin and cheese katsu.

It starts cooking immediately after ordering and you have to wait 10 to 15 minutes, but I felt like it was taking longer because delivery orders kept coming in.

In the case of the special deep-fried meat cutlet, the batter was a little wet, and unlike other stores, the fat part was large and the meat was aged, so when you bit into the fat, you could feel the strong meaty flavor, so I understand the opinion that people got sick of it after one bite, but it didn't bother me too much.

The pork cutlet sauce felt like a thin, ready-made product, and the salad sauce was a yuzu sauce, but the taste of yuzu was vague, so I felt it wasn't as good as without it.
Also, some people left comments saying that the taste of radish kimchi is strange, but since it only tastes bitter from the radish and there is no taste of the seasoning, I recommend not eating it.

In the case of cheese katsu, I don't know why they added ground pepper. At first, I couldn't really taste the cheese katsu because I could only smell the pepper to the point where I thought they had ground the pepper to cover up the poor quality, but after it cooled down and I tried it, the quality of the cheese katsu wasn't that bad. However, if I visit again, I don't think I will order cheese katsu.

People who are not used to greasy food may be able to eat it without leaving a little bit of the fat behind.
For those who live nearby, delivery is also available, so I recommend ordering it without waiting.

I have no intention of returning yet.

reviews.author: Chanjai Park
reviews.text: It feels like a small neighborhood alley restaurant. This is a Japanese-style ramen restaurant that is already known to local residents and especially young students. In most cases, similar businesses use rich pork bones as their base, but the ramen here is dominated by the flavor of chicken broth. Those who like the greasy and savory taste of pork may have different opinions about the broth here, which is like a slightly rich chicken soup, but I like the cleanliness of the broth being carefully brewed at home, rather than the taste that seems to have been brought out to the limit with seasonings supplied from a factory. I personally like Japanese ramen, but it's so high in calories that I feel like I'm so full that I can't even eat a snack after eating a bowl, but the portions here are just enough for an adult man to leave enough room for dessert, so this restaurant is perfect for enjoying gourmet food while trying other menus in the area. The staff were friendly, and although the interior had narrow seating arrangements optimized for solo dining, the turnover rate was fast, so I was able to eat right away with a short waiting time.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in ramen

A ramen restaurant located at the entrance of an alley.
This place sells tonkotsu and jiro ramen.
Personally, I pass on the orthodox Giro system because it is so good.
One of the best menus, 8,000 won
I ordered and tried tonkotsu ramen.
A pork smell that I couldn't detect in the store.
It was quite interesting to see what it felt like in ramen.
How can they get rid of the smell of pigs in the store like this?
The unique pork smell of tonkotsu was pleasant.
It feels like it goes well with thick soup.
The noodles are thin and have a nice texture.
Ichiran is a style that you will be satisfied with if you like it.
If you request it, they will give you a free bowl of rice.
You must take it and eat it.
Eating rice with rich tonkotsu
Personally, I find it the most satisfying.
You can eat pickled radish as a side dish.
It makes the greasy soup clear.
It seems like the perfect combination.

The store is smaller than expected,
There aren't many tables so during peak hours.
It feels like there will be some waiting.
There was plenty of time when I visited at 8 o'clock on a weekday.
Order at the kiosk at the entrance,
It is a style in which seats are assigned.
You can get garlic and rice upon request.
Tonkotsu ramen price including rice
This is good value for money.

Rice is the formula for tonkotsu~
